To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in utero cell and genetic therapies are promising approaches to treat inherited diseases, however, they are limited by the development of an anti-transgene humoral and cellular immune responses.

the in utero transplantation of fetal liver cells transduced ex vivo with a lentiviral reporter vector leads to a humoral and a cellular immunoresponse that limit the hematopoietic reconstitution of the recipients and the mothers.
in utero cell and/or gene therapies constitute alternative approaches to the postnatal treatments of inherited diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential of fetal liver cells for in utero gene therapies and the immune responses associated with the use of lentiviral vectors.
the development of in utero gene therapies.
the development of a new approach to treat diseases of the blood and immune system by using fetal stem cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transduction conditions that led to high transduction efficiency were associated with poor hematopoietic reconstitution and the detection of an immune response against the transgene.
the in utero transplantation with fetal liver cells transduced with lentiviral vectors is not a safe strategy for gene therapy of hematopoietic disorders.
the transgene itself can be a limiting factor for engraftment in prenatal transplantation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in utero gene therapy is an attractive alternative to the postnatal therapy of inherited diseases, but the immunoresponse against transgenic protein should be carefully studied to avoid rejection of the transduced cells.

the in utero transplantation of hematopoietic stem cells transduced with a retroviral vector expressing the green fluorescent protein (GFP) was associated with a humoral and cell-mediated immunoresponse against GFP in the transplanted mice and their mothers.

in utero cell and/or gene therapies are still a promising alternative for the treatment of inherited diseases, but the potential immunological response against the transgenic product must be taken into account in future protocols.

, when transduction conditions are optimized, the humoral and cellular responses against transgene products can be a limiting factor for the engraftment efficiency of fetal liver cells in in utero transplantation protocols.
the immune response against the transgene may be an issue for in utero gene therapy.
the use of a transgenic marker to assess gene transfer in prenatal gene therapy experiments could lead to misleading results.
